questions.q: Why does Caldwell's Priority Lookup Rule calculate company-wide Meridian impact to Priority 1 automatically, instead of letting an agent decide severity in the moment?
options: Because the lookup rule only applies to non-critical systems
Because consistent, platform-calculated Priority removes guesswork under pressure and feeds the one-hour resolution commitment reliably
Because manual Priority selection is faster for agents than a lookup rule
Because Priority 1 can only ever be set manually on the incident form
questions.explain: A calculated Priority keeps the one-hour target meaningful across every agent and every shift, instead of depending on individual judgment in a crisis.

questions.q: Why is the Major Incident trigger in this lesson scoped specifically to 'Priority 1 against Meridian' rather than every Priority 1 incident platform-wide?
options: Because Meridian incidents are actually always Priority 2 or lower
Because Major Incident process cannot technically be scoped to a specific Configuration Item
Because other Priority 1 incidents never require any kind of escalation
Because the VP's one-hour commitment and bridge-call communication cadence were specifically about Meridian, not every critical incident company-wide
questions.explain: The lesson scopes the Major Incident trigger to the exact requirement that drove it — matching the stakeholder's specific ask instead of a blanket rule.

questions.q: What does populating `problem_id` on each of the six Line 3 Incidents actually accomplish?
options: It links all six to one shared Problem investigation instead of treating each as a separate, disconnected issue
It converts each Incident into its own separate Problem record
It automatically resolves all six Incidents without any investigation
It deletes the duplicate Incident records from the table
questions.explain: Linking recurring Incidents to one Problem is exactly what stops repeat tickets from each triggering a fresh, redundant investigation.

questions.q: Once the network team finds the failing switch port causing the Line 3 symptom, what happens to `root_cause` on the Problem record?
options: It's set as a reference to the specific switch's `cmdb_ci` record, making the cause a structured, reportable data point
It's automatically deleted once the Problem is marked Resolved
It's left blank since `cause_notes` already describes the issue
It's set to the Incident record that was opened first
questions.explain: A reference-field root_cause turns 'what broke' into something you can actually report on, like which CI has caused the most Problems.

questions.q: Why can a routine, already-templated monthly Meridian patch still run as a Standard change, even though Meridian itself is treated as high-risk for Normal changes?
options: Because Meridian's risk rating only applies to Incident Management, not Change
Because CAB approval is required for every Standard change regardless of risk
Because Standard changes never apply to any production system
Because that specific, repeatable patch action was already reviewed and authorized once at template-creation time, so it doesn't need re-approval every run
questions.explain: Standard change status reflects that the authorization work happened once, up front, for the template — not that the underlying system is low-risk.
